mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (عرفا): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (المرسلات), which are the winds sent one after another. Whoever makes (المرسلات) the angels makes (عرفا) accusative on the basis of omitting the preposition, i.e. "Allah sends them with (العرف)", i.e. with what is right (المعروف).

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (عصفا) and (نشرا): two emphatic maṣdars (verbal nouns).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (ذكرا): a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying (عذرا أو نذرا): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). Whoever reads the dhāl with ḍamma makes it the plural of (عذير) and (نذير), in the sense of "excusing" and "warning". Whoever makes the dhāl vowelless, it may be lightened from the ḍamma form, in the sense of "excusing" and "warning", as He said (فكيف كان نكير), i.e. "My disapproval of them", i.e. the outcome of that. It may also be not lightened, its vowellessness being original, as a maṣdar on the pattern of (شكر).

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying (إنما توعدون لواقع): (ما) is the noun of (إن) and (لواقع) is the khabar (predicate). The hāʾ is omitted from (توعدون), and with it the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما) is completed; its implied form is (توعدونه). Its omission from the ṣila is good because of the length of the noun; close to it is its omission from an adjective; and its omission from a khabar is not permissible except in poetry. (إن) [with its clause] is the answer to the preceding oath.
His saying (فإذا النجوم طمست): (النجوم) is, according to the Basrans, nominative by an implied verb, because (إذا) carries the meaning of a conditional, so it is more fitting with the verb. Its like is (إذا الشمس كورت), (إذا السماء انشقت) and (إذا السماء انفطرت), and it is frequent in the Qur'an. The Kufans said: what follows (إذا) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what comes after it is the khabar. The answer of (إذا) in His saying, the Exalted (فإذا النجوم) is omitted, its implied form being "the decision will take place". It is also said that its answer is (ويل يومئذ للمكذبين).

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying (ليوم الفصل): the lām is attached to an implied verb, its implied form being "they were deferred for the Day of Decision". It is also said that it is a badal (substitute) from (أي) [Translator's note: i.e. from (لأي يوم)] with the preposition repeated. It is also said that the lām means (إلى) "until".

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying (وما أدراك ما يوم الفصل): it was mentioned before, in al-Ḥāqqa and elsewhere.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying (ويل يومئذ للمكذبين): (ويل), wherever it occurs in this sūra and what resembles it, is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يومئذ) is an adverbial governed by the meaning of (ويل), and (للمكذبين) is the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His saying (كفاتا): the second object of (نجعل), because it means "We make into" (نصير).
His saying (أحياء وأمواتا): two ḥāls (circumstantials), i.e. the earth gathers them in these two states; (الكفت) is gathering. It is also said that it is accusative governed by (كفات), i.e. it gathers the living and the dead, i.e. it holds them, living on its surface and dead in its interior.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying (هذا يوم لا ينطقون): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), the reference being to the day. Al-Aʿmash and others read (يوم) with fatḥa; so it may be indeclinable (mabnī) according to the Kufans because it is annexed to the verb, while being nominative in meaning. It may also be in the position of the accusative, the reference being to something other than the day. And the fatḥa may be an inflection [of the accusative], which is the school of the Basrans, because the verb is declinable, and according to the Basrans it is made indeclinable only when annexed to an indeclinable word; so the reference is to something other than the day, and it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ in every case.

mekki-muskil:44-44.t:
His saying (كذلك نجزي): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a recompense like that We recompense".
His saying (وتمتعوا قليلا): (قليلا) is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar [Translator's note: printed «لصدر»] or of an omitted adverbial, its implied form being "and enjoy a little enjoyment" or "for a little time". It is accusative by (تمتعوا) in both aspects, except that once it is a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) and once a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
